text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Prime Minister John Howard attacked executives yesterday, claiming they should accept wage restraint as their workers do in order to maintain favourable interest rates. Howard said the interest rate outlook appeared positive due to the restraint and he said there were hopes of an early rate cut. Page 1.

Singapore's High Commissioner, Lieutenant General Winston Choo, has warned that anti-Asian comments by Independent MP Pauline Hanson may damage Asian relations and ultimately affect tourism, education and exports in Australia. The warning came as Prime Miniter John Howard faced criticism from China's state-run press for not condemning Hanson's comments. Page 2.

In a move which will boost electrical workers' pay packets by 19.4 percent over the next three years, Victorian electrical contractors have conceded a wage deal to be finalised between the Communications, Electrical and Plumbing Union and the National Elctrical Contractors Association today. The deal is expected to apply to about 6,000 workers in Victoria. Page 3.

In a last-ditch effort, the ACTU has urged the Australian Democrats to revisit aspects of their agreement with the Howard government on industrial relations reform. The plea came after ACTU president Jennie George's call for the party to review areas of the deal where agreed provisions could leave workers worse off. Democrats Leader Cheryl Kernot stated on Monday she would not break her deal with the government. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Responding to growing concern that Queensland Independent MP Pauline Hanson's attacks on Asian immigration are threatening Australia's relations with its Asian neighbours, the federal Government is mounting a comprehensive exercise in damage control, with Prime Minister John Howard denouncing racism in Parliament yesterday. Page 1.

The minority Queensland government will be left open to a no-confidence motion in Parliament today following the shock resignation of the head of the Criminal Justice Commission inquiry into alleged electoral bribery by the National Party, Ken Carruthers. Carruthers announced his decision at a special hearing yesterday, saying he had faced political interference and threats of jail. Page 1.

Following fresh evidence that business executives' salary gains have accelerated as wage increases won by ordinary employees have eased, the Federal government has criticised the extravagant pay rises, saying they should set a better example to workers and warning they are jeopardising the chances of a further interest rate cut. Page 1.

Under a new Federal government plan to tackle the oversupply of doctors, which has won the approval of Australian Medical Association president Keith Woollard, foreign doctors arriving from next year will be banned from private practice for 10 years, meaning they will not be given the Medicare provider numbers required to establish a general practice. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Prime Minister John Howard has described editorials in leading newspapers across South-East Asia - which criticised him for not taking a firmer stand against Queensland Independent MP Pauline Hanson - as "deliberately misrepresenting" his views on race but he told his colleagues he did not plan on giving in to growing pressure to directly tackle Hanson on her views. Page 1.

Following the shock announcement yesterday that Ken Carruthers QC, the commissioner conducting an inquiry into a secret deal between the Coalition and the Queensland Police Union, was resigning, the Queensland government will battle a no-confidence motion in Parliament today. Page 1.

Under changes to be recommended by the Wood Royal Commission next week, Commissioner Peter Ryan will become the most powerful New South Wales police chief in decades, leaving him unfettered in selecting his new management team from outside the force and taking key powers from the Police Board. Page 1.

The Howard Government has given its support to an extensive environmental experiment, proposed by the CRC Research Centre at James Cook University, to study the impact of commercial fishing and recreational fishing on 24 areas in the Great Barrier Reef, including some of the most highly protected areas. Page 3.
THE AGE

One day after it was revealed thatColes Myer chief executive Peter Bartels' salary had increased by A$1 million, Prime Minister John Howard issued a firm warning to business leaders around the country to restrain pay rises. Howard said there needed to be "equality of sacrifice" and that wage restraint was the key to an early cut in interest rates. Page 1.

Eight bidders, including Hudson Conway and the Melbourne City Council, will fight for the A$1 billion Melbourne Airport. Bidders will face a legal process this week to ensure each is financially capable to meet the tender. The property's privatisation has attracted other bidders including, Southern Cross Airports, Australia Development Group and Australia Pacific Airports. Page 1.

Two boys, aged eight and five, who were found dead in a car at their Northwood Road home on Monday, were being monitored by child protection authorities, it was revealed. The children were considered unstable after the suicide of their father last year, but monitoring stopped in January because they were believed to be out of threat. Police believe the boys were poisoned. Page 1.

After the Federal government declared there were too many doctors in Australia, a 10-year moratorium has been designed which bans immigrant doctors from practising as GPs. Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge said the 600 doctors arriving from overseas were creating a large oversupply of doctors. Under the new ban, which will come into play on January 1, immigrant doctors will be prevented from accessing provider numbers for 10 years. Page 1.
